protocol: These videos are never used to tune the checker. Development uses bench/sources.json only.
Held-out runs write under runs/holdout/; only the totals command reads them during development.
Each held-out grading is recorded here with the checker version it graded; a grading is spent once read.
Selection: a seeded random draw (seed below) from two pools fixed by the rules below, by title and metadata only.

Publication: the grading's evidence (references, cut points, planted-mistake plans with their truth, every raw model response and request as sent, the cost ledger, the claimed results; no video) is committed under bench/holdout-evidence/, and `python -m watchverify.cli bench-replay bench/holdout-evidence` re-scores it offline through the checker's own code and exits non-zero on any mismatch.

The correct-performance case is a second check of the expert's own clip, graded against the self-check's marks; the self-check itself is calibration, not a graded result (re-scored with its own marks it cannot fail).

pool_rules.laptops: Commons search results titled 'How to open ...', CC BY/BY-SA/CC0, 60 to 900 s, minus every video used in development
pool_rules.non_laptop: Commons search results for soldering, bicycle repair, sewing machine, woodworking, plumbing, how to repair, how to install; licence and length as above; title names a hands-on procedure on a physical object; software installs and talks excluded
